nfd.notice: This text is NFD (decomposed jamo), common in file names created on macOS. Results below are computed after converting to NFC.

koreanSyllable.romanNote: Follows the Revised Romanization of Korean: liaison, consonant assimilation, palatalization and h-aspiration are applied; tensing is not written, per the rules. ㄴ-insertion and some compound exceptions need word meaning and are not applied. For personal names, separate surname and given name with a space.

compose.title: Compose jamo
compose.desc: Assemble separate jamo or Dubeolsik keyboard keys into Hangul syllables. Compound vowels and final clusters are merged automatically.

josa.title: Particle picker
josa.desc: Chooses the Korean particle from the final consonant of the last syllable ('로' after ㄹ; digits are read aloud, e.g. 3 = 삼). Click to copy.

koreanSyllable.title: Korean Syllable Decomposer
koreanSyllable.description: Extract initial consonants, split and compose jamo, romanize, and pick particles, all live as you type.

howItWorks.title: How it works
items: The 11,172 precomposed Hangul syllables start at U+AC00. Code = 0xAC00 + (initial×21 + medial)×28 + final.
Initial = (code − 0xAC00) ÷ 588, medial = (code − 0xAC00) % 588 ÷ 28, final = (code − 0xAC00) % 28. A final of 0 means no batchim.
Composition uses the same automaton as a Dubeolsik IME: ㅇㅏㄴㅈㅏ becomes '안자'; type ㅇㅏㄴㅈㅇㅏ for '앉아'.
Romanization applies sound changes between a batchim and the next initial within each word (baengma, silla, gachi, joko), then maps letters per the official table.
NFD stores each syllable as separate conjoining jamo (U+1100 block). It looks identical but breaks search and comparison, so normalize to NFC.

structure.title: Korean Structure
items: Korean syllables consist of initial (consonant) + medial (vowel) + final (consonant)
19 initial consonants: ㄱ ㄲ ㄴ ㄷ ㄸ ㄹ ㅁ ㅂ ㅃ ㅅ ㅆ ㅇ ㅈ ㅉ ㅊ ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅎ
21 medial vowels: ㅏ ㅐ ㅑ ㅒ ㅓ ㅔ ㅕ ㅖ ㅗ ㅘ ㅙ ㅚ ㅛ ㅜ ㅝ ㅞ ㅟ ㅠ ㅡ ㅢ ㅣ
27 final consonants: (none) ㄱ ㄲ ㄳ ㄴ ㄵ ㄶ ㄷ ㄹ ...

whatIs.title: What is the Korean Syllable Decomposer?
whatIs.description: A tool that decomposes Korean (Hangul) text into its constituent jamo — initial consonant (초성), vowel (중성), and final consonant (종성) — or extracts only the initial consonants. Useful for implementing initial-consonant search in apps, generating quiz hints, extracting acronyms, and analyzing Hangul string structure, all based on the Unicode Hangul syllable block decomposition formula.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: Type or paste Korean text; initials, jamo, romanization and Unicode appear instantly.
Turn on 'Keep spaces/symbols' for quizzes, off for search indexes.
Turn on 'Split double jamo' to break ㄺ or ㅘ into Dubeolsik keystrokes.
Copy any output with its button; share the page URL to restore the same input.
Use 'Compose jamo' (ㅎㅏㄴ → 한, dkssud → 안녕) and the particle picker below.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: When building an initial-consonant search feature, use this tool to validate your extraction results and refine your regex patterns.
For initial-consonant quiz games or song lyrics hint features, the extracted initials can be used directly as the clue text.

The decomposition formula for a Hangul codepoint N (where N ≥ 0xAC00): initial = (N − 0xAC00) ÷ 588, vowel = ((N − 0xAC00) ÷ 28) % 21, final = (N − 0xAC00) % 28. Useful when implementing this in code.

items.q: What about English, digits and symbols?
items.a: Non-Hangul characters are kept as is. Turn off 'Keep spaces/symbols' to drop them from the initials output.

items.q: How do I match every word starting with ㄱ?
items.a: Syllables starting with ㄱ are 가 (U+AC00) to 깋 (U+AE4B), so use /[가-깋]/. ㄲ is a separate range (까–낗).

items.q: File names from a Mac show split jamo like ㅎㅏㄴㄱㅡㄹ.
items.a: macOS stores file names in NFD. Paste the text here; it is detected and 'Convert to NFC' fixes it.

items.q: Why does the romanization differ from my passport name?
items.a: Passport names keep your established spelling and do not apply sound changes between surname and given name. Enter names with a space between them.
